import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Define boundary between two media.", "Set points A and B.", "Ray intersects boundary at point P.", "Label angles relative to normal.", "Observe path changes with point P."]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Modeling", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        air = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/air.svg")
        water = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/water.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(air, "A5", scale_factor=0.3)

        # Geometric Elements
        boundary = Line(self.grid["C3"], self.grid["C6"], color="#0000FF")
        normal = DashedLine(self.grid["A4"], self.grid["F4"], color=WHITE)

        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20)
        point_b = Dot(self.grid["E5"], color=YELLOW)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20)
        point_p = Dot(self.grid["C4"], color=WHITE)
        label_p = Text("P", font_size=20)
        
        ray_in = Line(point_a.get_center(), point_p.get_center(), color=YELLOW)
        ray_out = Line(point_p.get_center(), point_b.get_center(), color=YELLOW)
        
        geometry_group = VGroup(boundary, normal, point_a, point_b, point_p, ray_in, ray_out)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#0000FF")

        self.place_at_grid(label_b, 'F5', scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.place_at_grid(label_p, 'D4', scale_factor=0.7)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Derivation", [
            "Express time as a function.",
            "Take derivative to minimize time.",
            "Derivative equals zero at minimum.",
            "Simplify expression using trigonometry.",
            "Result relates angles to velocities."
        ])
        
        # Define equations
        eq1 = MathTex(r"T(x) = \frac{\sqrt{y_1^2 + x^2}}{v_1} + \frac{\sqrt{y_2^2 + (D-x)^2}}{v_2}", font_size=32)
        eq2 = MathTex(r"\frac{dT}{dx} = \frac{x}{v_1\sqrt{y_1^2 + x^2}} - \frac{D-x}{v_2\sqrt{y_2^2 + (D-x)^2}}", font_size=32)
        eq3 = MathTex(r"\frac{x}{\sqrt{y_1^2 + x^2}} = \sin(\theta_1), \quad \frac{D-x}{\sqrt{y_2^2 + (D-x)^2}} = \sin(\theta_2)", font_size=32)
        eq4 = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta_1)}{v_1} = \frac{\sin(\theta_2)}{v_2}", font_size=40, color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(eq1, 'B2', 'B4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(eq1), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(eq2, 'D2', scale_factor=0.85)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq1.copy(), eq2), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(eq2), FadeOut(eq1))
        self.place_in_area(eq3, 'C2', 'C4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(eq3), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 & 5 ===
        self.place_at_grid(eq4, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(eq4), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Physics of Refraction: Deriving Snell's Law

sections.title: Introduction: The Archerfish Phenomenon
sections.content: Hook the audience with an animation of an archerfish aiming at an insect above the water. Explain that the fish perceives the light bending at the air-water interface, introducing the need for a mathematical rule to predict this path.
sections.example: An archerfish calculating the 'apparent' position of prey due to light refraction.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Fermat’s Principle of Least Time
sections.content: Introduce Fermat’s Principle: Light travels between two points along the path that requires the least time. Connect this to the concept of velocity: v = c/n (where n is the refractive index).
sections.example: Visualizing a lifeguard running on sand vs. swimming in water to reach a drowning swimmer in the shortest time.

sections.title: Geometric Modeling
sections.content: Present a coordinate plane with a boundary line. Define two points A (in medium 1) and B (in medium 2). Draw a path intersecting the boundary at point P. Label distances: x (horizontal distance), y1, y2 (vertical distances), and angles θ1, θ2 relative to the normal.
sections.example: A split-screen animation showing the light ray path changing as point P shifts across the interface.

sections.title: Mathematical Derivation
sections.content: Express the total time function T(x) = sqrt(y1^2 + x^2)/v1 + sqrt(y2^2 + (D-x)^2)/v2. Set the derivative dT/dx = 0 to minimize time. Show the geometric steps resulting in sin(θ1)/v1 = sin(θ2)/v2.
sections.example: Animated sliding equations where the derivative symbol d/dx simplifies to the ratio of the sines.

sections.title: Synthesis: Snell’s Law
sections.content: Substitute v = c/n into the result to reach n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2). Summarize that light bends to 'save time' because it moves slower in denser media.
sections.example: Final diagram showing a laser beam passing through a glass block, highlighting the relationship between the incident angle and refractive indices.
